obtainedAt.value: Wild encounters in the Pokémon Mansion on Cinnabar Island.

femaleDeterminesSpecies.value: The female parent determines the offspring's species.

withDitto.value: With a Ditto pair, the non-Ditto parent determines the offspring's species.

how.value: The father must already know the move — catch or hatch a male that has it, then pair him at the Day Care.

effect.value: Eggs hatch from steps taken. Covering those same steps on a bicycle takes less real time than walking.
effect.note: Self-evident in play: a bicycle covers the same step count in less wall-clock time. Not a rate, so a second source is not a measurement.

noEggRateBoostsReason: This game has no item or charm that raises how often eggs appear — Day Care compatibility alone sets the rate.

noEggShinyBoostsReason.value: The Masuda Method doesn't exist in this game — it was introduced in Generation IV — and the Shiny Charm came later still, in Generation V. Base odds are the only egg shiny odds here.

hatchMechanicExplainer.value: Leave two compatible Pokémon at the Four Island Day Care (the Route 5 Day Care only holds one, so it cannot produce eggs). After enough steps the Day-Care Man offers an Egg; how often that happens depends only on whether the parents share a species and Original Trainer — there is no Oval Charm or other rate boost here. Carry the Egg in your party and walk: it hatches at level 5. Flame Body does not shorten hatch steps in FireRed/LeafGreen (that starts in Emerald).

Dragon Dance.value: Raises the user's Attack and Speed by one stage each.

Blaze.value: When this Pokémon's HP is at or below one-third, the power of its Fire-type moves is boosted.

Intimidate.value: Lowers the Attack of opposing Pokémon when this Pokémon enters battle.

method.value: Eggs hatch from steps taken in the overworld.

unlockedAfter.value: the Elite Four, then Rainbow Pass access to Four Island (deliver the Ruby and Sapphire to Celio on One Island)
